'''Chinkoku-ji''' (鎮国寺) is a temple located in Yoshida, {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|en|Munakata, Fukuoka|qid=Q819603|lt=Munakata City}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|qid=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}}. Its sect is {{ill|Shingon Omuro School|ja|真言宗御室派|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q420739}}, and it is recognized as a Special Head Temple. The mountain name is Byōbu-yama, and its principal image is {{ill|Vairocana|en|Vairocana|qid=Q239847|lt=Dainichi Nyorai}}. It is designated as the 31st sacred site of the {{ill|33 pilgrimage sites of Kyūshū-Saigoku|ja|九州西国霊場|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九州西国三十三箇所|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11370337}}, the 88th of the {{ill|Kyushu 88 Sacred Sites|ja|九州八十八箇所霊場|qid=Q140446063}}, the 34th of the {{ill|Kyushu 36 Fudō Sacred Sites|ja|九州三十六不動霊場|qid=Q140446064}}, and the 1st of the {{ill|Kyushu 33 Kannon Sacred Sites|ja|九州三十三観音霊場|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135550947}}. In former times, it served as the {{ill|Jingū-ji|en|Jingū-ji|qid=Q1074971|lt=Jingū-ji}} of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|qid=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha}}.
== Overview ==
According to temple legend, when {{ill|Kūkai|en|Kūkai|qid=Q222227|lt=Kobo Daishi}} set out on the 16th mission to Tang China aboard a Japanese envoy ship, he encountered a violent storm at sea. In his prayers to the guardian deities of the ocean – including the {{ill|Three Munakata Goddesses|ja|宗像三神|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宗像三女神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10948069}} – a manifestation of {{ill|Acala|en|Acala|qid=Q337624|lt=Fudō Myōō}} appeared among the waves and, wielding a sharp sword in his right hand, dispersed the surging waters to calm the storm, allowing him to safely reach Tang.
Subsequently, in Chang'an (present-day {{ill|Xi'an|ja|西安|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 西安市|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5826}}), he received the secret esoteric teachings of Shingon from the priest Keika of {{ill|Qinglong Temple (Xi'an)|en|Qinglong Temple (Xi'an)|qid=Q10565990|lt=Qinglong Temple}}. In the year {{ill|806|en|806|qid=Q30021|lt=806}}, after arriving at Hakata and returning to Japan, he first paid his respects at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|qid=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha}}. At that time, upon witnessing auspicious clouds gathering over Byōbu-yama, he commenced his ritual practices within a rock cave in the inner sanctuary. There he received an oracle proclaiming, "This land is destined to be the principal sacred site for protecting the nation." Consequently, he established a temple and named it '''Byōbu-yama Chinkoku-ji'''. Around this period, Kūkai remained in Dazaifu for several years.
It is the private temple of {{ill|Tatebe Yūdō|ja|立部祐道}}, the 50th head priest of Munmuro-ha at Ninna-ji, and former chief of the sect. Additionally, his father, Tatebe Zuiyū, served as the 43rd head priest of Munmuro-ha.
== Temple Grounds ==
[[File:Purunus mume at Chinkokuji-Temple 01.JPG|thumb|Ume blossoms blooming in front of the main hall, February 2014]]
Situated on a small hill immediately east of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|qid=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha}}, across the {{ill|Tsuri River|ja|釣川|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11648228}}, the temple stands in a serene location. The grounds are planted with a diverse array of flowering trees, earning it the nickname “Temple of Flowers.”
The main hall was rebuilt in the 3rd year of the {{ill|Keian|fa|کی‌آن|fr|Ère Keian|ja|慶安|ko|게이안|ru|Кэйан|simple|Keian|sr|Кеиан|sv|Keian|th|เคอัง|tr|Keian|zh|慶安 (日本)|qid=Q1146135|lt=Keian era}} (1650) under the patronage of {{ill|Tadayuki Kuroda|ja|黒田忠之|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11678600}}, the second feudal lord of the Fukuoka Domain, and has been designated as a cultural property by Munakata City. The wooden standing statue of {{ill|Acala|en|Acala|qid=Q337624|lt=Fudō Myōō}}, a secret Buddha displayed only on April 28, is recognized as a National Important Cultural Property, and the group of statues in the Five Buddhas Hall is designated as a cultural property by Fukuoka Prefecture.
== Souvenirs ==
The specialty of Munakata City is the “Chinkoku” manju—a confection closely associated with Chinkoku-ji. It is produced by the confectionery shop Chinkoku Manju no Tsuzuka.
== Access ==
* From {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|cs|JR Kjúšú|de|Kyushu Railway Company|es|Kyushu Railway Company|fa|راه‌آهن کیوشو|fi|JR Kyūshū|fr|Kyushu Railway Company|hu|Kyushu Railway Company|id|Perusahaan Jalur Kereta Api Kyushu|it|Kyushu Railway Company|ja|九州旅客鉄道|jv|Kyushu Railway Company|ko|큐슈여객철도|nds|JR Kyūshū|nl|Kyushu Railway Company|pl|Kyushu Railway Company|pt|Kyushu Railway Company|ru|Kyushu Railway Company|th|บริษัทรถไฟคีวชู|tr|Kyushu Railway Company|ur|کیوشو ریلوے کمپنی|wuu|九州旅客铁道|zh|九州旅客鐵道|zh_yue|九州旅客鐵道|qid=Q498366}} on the {{ill|Kagoshima Main Line|en|Kagoshima Main Line|qid=Q1187520|lt=Kagoshima Main Line}}, board a {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11629843}} bound for Kaminato Wharf (神湊波止場) and alight at “Munakata Taisha-mae”; then walk for 17 minutes (1.4 km).
* By car, the temple is located 17 km from the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|de|Kyūshū-Autobahn|fr|Autoroute Kyūshū|ja|九州自動車道|ko|규슈 자동차도|nl|Kyushu-autosnelweg|zh|九州自動車道|qid=Q1060803|lt=Kyushu Expressway}} at the {{ill|Wakamiya interchange|ja|若宮インターチェンジ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1575782}}, or 16 km from the {{ill|Koga interchange|ja|古賀インターチェンジ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1577981}}.
* Parking is available.
